I'm noticing that `intel_display_suspend` is actually `intel_display_driver_suspend` in this codebase, and I'm tracing through the call chain to see which functions invoke `i915_drm_suspend` — so far I've found `i915_pm_freeze` and `i915_driver_shutdown` calling it, and I'm checking what else might be calling into `i915_g`.

Looking at the runtime suspend path, `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` doesn't actually exist — the runtime callback is `intel_runtime_suspend` instead.
## 1. PCI PM callbacks → `i915_pm_suspend`

`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c`:
```
static struct pci_driver i915_pci_driver = { .driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops, ... }
```

`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c` — `i915_pm_ops` entries that reach `i915_pm_suspend`:

```
.suspend  = i915_pm_suspend      <-- direct
.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend      <-- same function reused (aliased)
```

Those are the **only two** PM-op slots bound to `i915_pm_suspend`. Everything else is a sibling, not a caller:

```
.prepare        = i915_pm_prepare
.suspend_late   = i915_pm_suspend_late
.suspend_noirq  = i915_pm_suspend_noirq
.freeze         = i915_pm_freeze          (calls i915_drm_suspend directly, NOT i915_pm_suspend)
.freeze_late    = i915_pm_freeze_late
.poweroff_late  = i915_pm_poweroff_late
.poweroff_noirq = i915_pm_poweroff_noirq
.thaw_early/.thaw/.restore_early/.restore -> i915_pm_resume_early / i915_pm_resume
```

Full chain (both entry points converge):

```
PCI core (dev_pm_ops)
  ├─ .suspend  ──┐
  └─ .poweroff ──┴─> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
                        i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
                        └─> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
                              ├─ dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
                              ├─ display  = dev_priv->display
                              ├─ intel_display_driver_disable_user_access(display)
                              ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)   <-- "display suspend"
                              ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display)
                              ├─ intel_dpt_suspend(display)
                              ├─ i915_gem_suspend(i915)
                              └─ intel_opregion_suspend(display, opregion_target_state)
```

Parallel (non-`i915_pm_suspend`) paths that land on the same `i915_drm_suspend`:
```
.freeze  -> i915_pm_freeze     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
i915_driver_shutdown           -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm) + i915_drm_suspend_late(..., true)
```

## 2. Which of those callers also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None.** There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in the tree. The runtime-PM hook is a *separate* callback:

```
i915_pm_ops.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend
```

`intel_runtime_suspend` is an independent leaf from the PCI runtime-PM core; neither `i915_pm_suspend`, `i915_pm_freeze`, nor `i915_driver_shutdown` invoke it. It has its own body:
```
intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)
  dev_priv = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  ├─ i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
  ├─ for_each_gt: intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
  └─ intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
```
So the system-suspend and runtime-suspend chains are fully disjoint — they only share the `i915_pm_ops` struct.

## 3. `dev_priv` data flow: `i915_drm_suspend` → display suspend

Note the modern name is **`intel_display_driver_suspend`** (`display/intel_display_driver.c`); a bare `intel_display_suspend` no longer exists.

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
        │  kdev  ──kdev_to_i915()──>  struct drm_i915_private *i915
        ▼
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)          # dev == &i915->drm
        │
        │  struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
        │        (container_of on the embedded drm_device — the same object,
        │         so dev_priv == the i915 passed in by i915_pm_suspend)
        │
        │  struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
        │        (pointer stored during probe:
        │           display = intel_display_device_probe(pdev, &parent);
        │           i915->display = display;)
        ▼
intel_display_driver_suspend(struct intel_display *display)
        │  dev_priv is NOT forwarded — it is *narrowed* to display
        └─ state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
           intel_dp_mst_suspend(display)
```

Data-flow summary: `struct device *kdev` → `drm_i915_private *dev_priv` (via `kdev_to_i915` / `to_i915`) → field deref `dev_priv->display` → `struct intel_display *`. The display layer receives **only** `display`, never `dev_priv`; it re-derives DRM state through `display->drm`. This is the deliberate i915↔display decoupling (`display_member.h` / `display_parent_interface.h` includes at the top of `i915_driver.c`).
